about: The labelled prompts for the benchmark. on_topic: prompts about something recorded in the vault, each naming the memory items (path#heading) recall must find. off_topic: ordinary coding prompts that should inject nothing. continuation: short follow-ups that should inject nothing. needles: the labelled memories, written into the seeded vault at those items. The prompt lists are the 20 plus 20 of the token usage report (2026-10-27).

needles.text: Webhook delivery in billing retries with jittered backoff capped at 60 seconds, and every attempt carries the same idempotency key so a retry never charges twice.
needles.why: two customers were charged twice during the October incident

needles.text: The job queue in billing runs on Postgres 16.4; Maya Chen owns it and its runbook is wiki page 2207.
After the tenant schema migration the invoice export times out: the new tenant_id column has no index, so the export does a sequential scan. Fix: add an index on (tenant_id, created_at).
needles.why: it took a day to find the first time

needles.text: The invoice export runs in a background worker, never in the request path, so a slow export cannot time out the API.
Tomas Ruiz owns the staging environment runbook and approves every change to the staging cluster.
The billing cache layer returns stale data because the cache is invalidated before the database transaction commits; invalidate after commit.
needles.why: stale invoice totals reached two customers

needles.text: Rate limiting for the admin dashboard is a token bucket of 120 requests per minute per user, enforced in the gateway rather than in the app.
needles.why: the app servers cannot share counters

needles.text: Session storage moved from Redis 7 to Postgres in September; Redis is now only the read cache.
The nightly backfill query needs a partial index on events (created_at) where processed is false; build it with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.
Stripe double charges on retry in checkout when the idempotency key is generated per attempt; generate it once per order and reuse it on every retry.
needles.why: refunds cost a week of support time

needles.text: Checkout stores the Stripe idempotency key on the order row before the first charge attempt.
The data pipeline lockfile gets corrupted when two CI jobs run the dependency compile step at once; serialise those jobs with a concurrency group.
Audit logging keeps every billing change for seven years in an append-only table that no service can update or delete.
needles.why: legal asked for a seven year audit trail

needles.text: Release tagging for billing: tag vX.Y.Z on main only after the changelog entry is merged; the tagging script is scripts/release-tag.sh.
CSV imports fail on rows with a null created_at; default those rows to the import time and log their row numbers.
Tenant isolation: every query goes through a tenant-scoped repository, and Postgres row level security is the backstop.
needles.why: a missing tenant filter leaked one report in a test environment

needles.text: The load balancer returns 502 when the upstream keep-alive timeout is shorter than its own 60 seconds; set the upstream keep-alive to 65 seconds.
The load balancer idle timeout is 60 seconds on every environment.
Schema migrations run with lock_timeout 5s and statement_timeout 60s.
needles.why: a migration once blocked writes for twenty minutes

needles.text: Background retries in the notifications service use Celery with five attempts and exponential backoff from 30 seconds; failures go to a dead letter queue that support reviews.
The report export publishes to the Kafka topic analytics.report-export.v2; the v1 topic is drained and read-only.
A PR that changes feature flags in billing needs a rollout plan in its description and a reviewer from the billing on-call rotation.
needles.why: a flag flip once disabled invoicing for an hour

needles.text: The mobile push gateway sends through Firebase on Android and APNs on iOS, retries three times, and drops a device token after two hard bounces.
Push notifications go through our own gateway service, never straight from the app servers to the vendors.
needles.why: one place for rate limits and token cleanup
